Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across business and general-news outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid an espionage-tinged affair scandal, and the imminent Anthropic IPO that is being watched as a referendum on the AI trade. Secondary threads include a prolonged Microsoft global outage, Trump's upcoming three-way summit with Xi and Putin, and political fallout reaching into the Trump administration over Nvidia's China exports.

stories.headline: Nvidia scrambles to find a permanent CEO after Jensen Huang's ouster
stories.summary: Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned after revelations of multiple affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy; Fortune and Axios report the board has not yet picked a search firm and is weighing internal candidates like CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress and Huang's son-in-law Nico Caprez alongside external names like Tim Cook and Lisa Su.

stories.headline: Wall Street pitches investors on Anthropic's roadshow ahead of record IPO
stories.summary: Investment banks are touring investors to sell what could be the largest public offering ever, with Anthropic expected to begin trading Thursday at a valuation of roughly $1.33 trillion or more even as broader AI-market uncertainty deepens.

stories.headline: Trump to hold unprecedented three-way summit with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Trump will hold an unprecedented three-way meeting with China's Xi and Russia's Putin next week in China's tech hub of Shenzhen; CNBC reports senior U.S. officials say Trump does not plan to raise the Nvidia/Huang Chinese-spy allegations during the trip.

stories.headline: Lutnick faces congressional pressure over handling of Nvidia's China chip exports
stories.summary: Trump's top economic advisers have clashed over Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's handling of an investigation into whether Megaspeed, the company central to the Huang scandal, breached U.S. export restrictions; Puck reports Lutnick will testify before Congress amid allegations he resisted a crackdown.

stories.headline: Oil market stays well-supplied despite ongoing tanker attacks tied to Iran
stories.summary: More than eight months into the Iran conflict, tankers near the Strait of Hormuz continue to be attacked even as crude supply remains ample, while WSJ separately notes oil prices rebounded after Trump said the U.S. doesn't need a deal with Iran.

stories.headline: Centrica and Equinor advance in bidding for Germany's Uniper
stories.summary: Centrica and Equinor are among companies advancing to the second round of the sale process for Germany's state-backed energy group Uniper, according to people familiar with the matter.

stories.headline: CVS weighs a breakup of its drugstore business
stories.summary: WSJ reports that spinning off CVS's drugstores won't quiet the company's critics in Washington, but could still leave shareholders with a more valuable company.

Business.gaps: The Information did not surface any distinct recent stories in search; Business Insider blocks web search and had no feed items provided, so it could not be included.

US politics.overview: US political coverage right now is dominated by the fallout from the Nov. 3 midterm blue wave: a rare and increasingly bitter fight over Senate Democratic leadership between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen, and the widening Jensen Huang/Nvidia spy scandal that has ensnared Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Outlets are also tracking a historic Alaska governor's flip, a brief nationwide FAA ground stop, a Trump-Putin-Xi summit announcement, and new Supreme Court and Medicaid policy developments.

stories.headline: Van Hollen's insurgent challenge to Schumer scrambles Senate Democratic leadership race
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is rapidly picking up endorsements, including from Bernie Sanders and several Democratic senators-elect, in his bid to oust Chuck Schumer as Senate Democratic leader ahead of a Dec. 1 secret-ballot vote, exposing deep divisions despite the party's sweeping midterm win.

stories.headline: Nvidia spy scandal fallout hits Commerce Secretary Lutnick
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports Trump's top economic advisers are clashing over Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's handling of Nvidia amid the Jensen Huang affair scandal, as the Commerce Department faces scrutiny over possible export-control breaches by Megaspeed.

stories.headline: Democrat flips Alaska governor's office for first time in two decades
stories.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins' projected win makes him Alaska's youngest-ever governor and the first Democrat to hold the office in over 20 years, a race Cook Political Report had shifted from toss-up to lean Democrat ahead of the vote.

stories.headline: FAA's nationwide ground stop reignites air traffic control funding fight
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and DHS's Markwayne Mullin used a Friday briefing on the nationwide FAA ground stop to renew demands for a roughly $50 billion overhaul of the country's aging air traffic control systems.

stories.headline: Trump to hold first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi
stories.summary: President Trump plans to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping together on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in China, an unprecedented three-way sit-down.

stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear Trump's asylum suspension case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to take up the Trump administration's border "invasion" authority that suspended asylum processing, setting up a major test of executive power over immigration.

stories.headline: Administration delays Medicaid work-requirement enforcement by six months
stories.summary: The federal government will let states push back implementation of a Medicaid work requirement from January to July, delaying a policy that would have required many low-income adults to prove employment to keep coverage.

stories.headline: Lauren Boebert loses House seat in another Colorado Democratic flip
stories.summary: Republican firebrand Rep. Lauren Boebert was projected to lose her Colorado seat to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, part of the broader midterm wave that cost the GOP its House majority.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report could not be confirmed with outlet-specific coverage from the last 24-48 hours beyond general midterm/Alaska analysis found via search; Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian were limited to the feed items provided since they block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI coverage over the last 24-48 hours is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and its implications for AI funding, China chip smuggling, and corporate governance, alongside Anthropic's blockbuster IPO roadshow. A global Microsoft 365 outage and a nationwide FAA ground stop also drew heavy cross-outlet attention as infrastructure reliability stories, while OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet launch and new frontier model releases from Google and Anthropic continued the steady drumbeat of AI product news.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia resignation reverberates across AI industry
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports that founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations now that Huang, who poured tens of billions into AI startups, is gone, while outlets including the WSJ and FT examine Nvidia's legal exposure and the hunt for a successor (Arm's Rene Haas has reportedly been approached). The Information separately reports Huang's son-in-law's rise inside Nvidia and that Nvidia board members have long personal ties to him, complicating succession.

stories.headline: Anthropic proceeds with IPO roadshow amid market jitters
stories.summary: Investment banks are pitching investors on what could be the largest public offering ever, with Anthropic targeting a valuation north of $1 trillion; The Decoder reports banks are barring Chinese and Hong Kong investors from participating due to U.S. export-control rules.

stories.headline: Microsoft 365 services restored after prolonged global outage
stories.summary: Microsoft said all its 365 products are fully operational again after an outage disrupted email, messaging and other services for governments, hospitals, traders and businesses worldwide for roughly two days; the Guardian reports Microsoft issued an apology, noting potential billion-dollar impact in Australia alone.

stories.headline: FAA nationwide ground stop halts US flights before being lifted
stories.summary: Takeoffs across the US largely stopped Friday after the FAA issued its third-ever nationwide ground stop, which officials attributed to communications issues at air traffic control centers and obsolete equipment, before lifting it hours later.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent-driven purchases
stories.summary: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet, letting its Dots agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and other surfaces complete purchases with user approval, rolling out first to U.S. Pro subscribers; The Decoder notes this is OpenAI's second attempt at AI shopping after scrapping its earlier Instant Checkout feature.

stories.headline: China's top AI models found trained on export-banned Nvidia chips
stories.summary: New forensic research cited by TechCrunch and The Register shows China's most advanced AI models, including from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group, were trained using banned Nvidia Blackwell chips despite export controls, adding pressure to the ongoing Huang scandal.

stories.headline: Google and Anthropic push out new models as the AI release cycle accelerates
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and pricier successor to its Flash model line aimed at coding and agent workflows, while Anthropic separately rolled out a Claude feature for Google Meet and faster versions of its Fable and Mythos models as competition over price and speed intensifies.

stories.headline: OpenAI board member warns of AI 'takeover' risk within months
stories.summary: An OpenAI board member cautioned that an AI 'takeover' of society could be only months away, tracing a path from reward hacking in AI systems to potentially catastrophic outcomes, according to Ars Technica's report.

Tech & AI.gaps: The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian block web search, so coverage for those outlets reflects only the provided feed items, not a full check of their current front pages. No distinct recent items were found for Google DeepMind beyond its standard Gemini product page.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the closing days of COP31 in Antalya, the ripple effects of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on AI-driven power demand, and continued volatility in oil markets tied to the Iran conflict. U.S.-focused outlets are also tracking a wave of utility and regulatory fights -- from California's climate disclosure laws to massive gas/nuclear capex plans -- as the industry grapples with surging data-center electricity demand.

stories.headline: UN chief delivers blistering COP31 closing message as summit wraps in Antalya
stories.summary: In what may be his final address as UN Secretary-General, António Guterres accused fossil fuel interests of profiting while worsening the climate crisis, a headline moment from COP31 in Antalya; Carbon Brief separately published UK climate envoy Ed Miliband's answers to reader questions from the summit.

stories.headline: China pledges to meet all new power demand with clean energy by 2030
stories.summary: State broadcaster CCTV reported that China is expected to cover all growth in electricity demand with new clean-energy generation by 2030, a pledge that landed alongside Heatmap's report that Beijing signed a $15 billion deal to supply Turkey with solar, wind, storage and transmission capacity at COP31.

stories.headline: Oil market stays oversupplied even as Iran tanker attacks and Trump's Iran comments stoke volatility
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports crude supplies remain ample despite months of Iranian attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, while WSJ notes prices rebounded after President Trump said the U.S. doesn't need a deal with Iran, reinjecting risk premium into the market.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit sends shockwaves through the AI power buildout
stories.summary: Heatmap reports Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation is adding fresh uncertainty to the AI boom just as the sector's data-center energy deals accelerate; Latitude Media is separately tracking the energy-market fallout from the shakeup.

stories.headline: Appeals court splits on California's corporate climate disclosure laws
stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit allowed California's SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 emissions reporting requirements to proceed while halting enforcement of Scope 3 disclosure and a related climate-risk law, leaving companies in limbo over compliance timelines.

stories.headline: EIA: Renewables, not coal, to absorb most new U.S. power demand next year
stories.summary: New EIA projections show the power sector could add more than 26 GW of battery storage next year, with renewables expected to supply almost a quarter of generation as coal burn continues to decline.

stories.headline: Venezuela vows to finish Colombia pipeline repairs by March
stories.summary: Venezuela committed to completing repairs on a key binational pipeline with Colombia by March, a move that would help its neighbor offset dwindling oil reserves.

stories.headline: Southern Co. unveils roughly $100B capex plan centered on gas and nuclear
stories.summary: Southern Co. executives outlined a roughly $100 billion spending plan on natural gas, nuclear and other infrastructure, with CEO Chris Womack downplaying the risk that political shifts in Washington could derail the company's growth strategy.

Energy.gaps: No recent (last 24-48h) articles could be found for E&E News or Argus Media beyond general site/about pages. Reuters, FT, and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so they are not represented here. NYT's only feed item (a Panama port story) was unrelated to energy/climate and was excluded.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by preparations for next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Trump, Xi and Putin are set for an unprecedented three-way meeting, alongside fallout from the Nvidia/Jensen Huang espionage scandal and its ripple effects on China's chip supply chain. Business and economy outlets are also tracking China's trade resilience, market-stability warnings from regulators, and a wave of Chinese chip and EV company listings and launches.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
stories.summary: The White House confirmed the first-ever three-way meeting between the US, Russian and Chinese leaders will take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with Trump expected to raise nuclear arms reduction and Iran but not Ukraine.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal exposes China's chip-industry spy network
stories.summary: WSJ reports Beijing has run a vast intelligence operation targeting the tech industry, with US officials worried CEO Jensen Huang was ensnared before his exit; Rest of World and Nikkei note the affair is rattling China's AI chip supply chain, while Caixin says Beijing has dismissed the spying claims.

stories.headline: China's market regulator warns of global asset repricing risks
stories.summary: China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Wu Qing said global capital markets are undergoing a new round of repricing and rebalancing amid geopolitical tensions and policy uncertainty.

stories.headline: China's export engine keeps humming as annual trade surplus tops $1 trillion
stories.summary: Nikkei reports China's October exports stayed strong and the cumulative 2026 trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion even as Beijing works to ease tensions with major trading partners.

stories.headline: Chinese chipmakers rush to Hong Kong listings amid AI chip boom
stories.summary: Alibaba's chip unit T-Head is exploring a Hong Kong IPO, coming right after domestic GPU maker Denglin Technology's own Hong Kong debut raised HK$1.41 billion, underscoring investor appetite for China's homegrown AI chip sector.

stories.headline: Wanted Chinese businessman at center of Panama port controversy
stories.summary: The NYT profiles a Chinese businessman who built influence in Panama before selling a strategic port, and is now sought by Beijing after falling out of favor.

China.gaps: Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Pandaily (beyond AI product items) and Focus Taiwan returned no distinct recent lead stories beyond what's cited above; Reuters, AP, FT and The Economist had no relevant feed items provided and could not be searched directly.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the deepening Iran-US-Israel standoff, with near-daily tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and a drone strike on a US radar site in Bahrain, alongside reports that Trump may pause further strikes on Iran. Israeli outlets are intensely focused on the post-election coalition scramble between Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, while business outlets track Gulf market reactions including UAE share buybacks and regional fallout from Nvidia's leadership turmoil.

stories.headline: Iran says tankers hit by mines as Hormuz attacks continue
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while trying to transit the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorized route, part of a pattern of near-weekly incidents since the war with the US began in February.

stories.headline: US says it shot down Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain, denies radar was destroyed
stories.summary: US Central Command said it intercepted two Iranian one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain with no damage or injuries, rejecting an IRGC claim that it had destroyed a US early-warning radar on the island in retaliation for a strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik.

stories.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot clash over coalition and Iran policy as unity push intensifies
stories.summary: Israeli outlets report that security officials see Netanyahu and his appointees pushing for renewed war with Iran while army chief Eyal Zamir remains isolated in opposition, even as Netanyahu renews unity-government appeals and Eisenkot's bloc negotiates with Haredi parties to form a government.

stories.headline: Trump reportedly weighing holding off on further Iran strikes
stories.summary: Al-Monitor's wire report says President Trump has told senior advisers he may refrain from attacking Iran again unless there are new provocations, a notable shift after months of tit-for-tat escalation.

stories.headline: Oil market stays well-supplied despite ongoing tanker attacks
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that despite more than eight months of Iranian attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, global crude markets remain oversupplied, limiting the price impact of the ongoing Gulf conflict.

stories.headline: UAE-listed firms turn to rare share buybacks after stock sell-offs
stories.summary: Six UAE-listed companies, most based in Abu Dhabi including IHC, Alpha Dhabi, Space42 and Borouge, have launched share buybacks following sustained stock sell-offs, an unusual move in a market that has traditionally favored dividends over buybacks.

stories.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi eye possible trilateral summit
stories.summary: Al-Monitor's wire coverage says the leaders of the US, Russia and China could meet as early as next week to discuss major global flashpoints, though Beijing is reportedly wary of hosting such a summit.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No current, non-outdated material could be found from Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Khaleej Times or Al Arabiya English via search; AP, FT, NYT and The Economist had no feed items and are search-blocked, so nothing could be reported for them.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage over the past 24-48 hours centers on security crises in the DRC and Sahel, the long-delayed South Sudanese elections, and Washington's deepening economic and diplomatic footprint in Africa (from a new DRC ambassador pick to trade and mining maneuvering). A parallel thread across business-focused outlets covers the fallout from a global Microsoft outage on African banks and corporate deal-making in Kenyan retail and Congolese mining.

stories.headline: DR Congo: At least 44 dead in attack by Islamic State-linked gunmen
stories.summary: The Allied Democratic Forces killed at least 44 people in a new raid, coming just days after the group killed 66 people in North Kivu, underscoring the deteriorating security situation in eastern Congo.

stories.headline: South Sudan postpones first-ever national elections until February
stories.summary: South Sudan's election commission pushed its first-ever national vote, originally expected in 2022, to 11 February, as voter registration began this week ahead of the long-delayed polls.

stories.headline: US-Africa: Trump picks pastor and early backer as US ambassador to the DRC
stories.summary: President Trump has nominated South Carolina preacher John Mark Burns, who has no diplomatic experience, to fill a DRC ambassadorship left vacant for nearly a year as Washington tightens its grip on Congo's cobalt sector.

stories.headline: Microsoft's 18-hour outage exposed South Africa's dependence on Big Tech
stories.summary: A global Microsoft cloud outage knocked out services for major South African institutions including Eskom, Absa and FlySafair, and TechCabal separately reported Kenyan banks and insurers lost email access for over 15 hours and had to fall back on WhatsApp and phone lines.

stories.headline: France escalates Algeria trade dispute to EU-level
stories.summary: Paris has asked the European Commission to investigate alleged Algerian non-compliance with the EU trade deal, accusing Algiers of an almost total blockade on French imports.

stories.headline: US, UK investors tighten grip on Kenya's $23.1bn retail industry despite China threat
stories.summary: Following Quickmart's oversubscribed IPO, foreign investors now control roughly 60% of Kenya's supermarket sector alongside Naivas and Carrefour, even as low-cost Chinese retailers mount fresh competition.

stories.headline: Barrick furloughs some employees at Congo mine as Ebola precaution
stories.summary: Barrick Mining is furloughing employees and subcontractors at its Kibali gold mine in DR Congo after officials reported two Ebola deaths in a nearby community, according to an internal memo cited by Reuters.

stories.headline: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for around 20 people, including journalists
stories.summary: The warrants target exiled journalists, activists, a former minister and ex-military officers who face terrorism-related charges, signaling a widening crackdown on dissent under the junta.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site returned only generic homepage/archive content with no specific recent Africa stories identifiable; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and no feed items were supplied for them, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days centers on major shakeups at legacy TV news divisions (CBS's Face the Nation, CNN's contract renewals under Skydance), a high-stakes Hollywood ownership lawsuit over 'Heat,' and continuing structural pressure on the news business from AI, funding cuts, and platform policy fights in markets from Indonesia to Canada.

stories.headline: Mary Hager and Anne Hsu depart CBS News' Face the Nation
stories.summary: Status reported that longtime 'Face the Nation' boss Mary Hager, a 35-year CBS veteran who also serves as executive editor of politics, is leaving the network, with executive producer Anne Hsu also departing to CBS's Hong Kong bureau.

stories.headline: CNN anchors Keilar and Ward face contract uncertainty under Skydance
stories.summary: Status reports that with their contracts nearing expiration under new owner Skydance, the futures of CNN anchors Brianna Keilar and Clarissa Ward are unclear, and network boss Mark Thompson and his deputies also remain without new deals.

stories.headline: New Regency sues Michael Mann over 'Heat' screenplay rights
stories.summary: New Regency has sued director Michael Mann as he seeks to reclaim copyright to the original 'Heat' screenplay ahead of shooting the long-awaited sequel 'Heat 2' in January, setting up a high-profile ownership fight.

stories.headline: Indonesia weighs copyright bill forcing Google and Meta to pay news publishers
stories.summary: Nieman Lab reports that representatives from Meta, TikTok and Google testified before Indonesia's parliament this week opposing a proposed copyright law that would require digital platforms to pay news publishers for aggregating their content.

stories.headline: Journalism organizations cancel conferences and cut staff amid funding crunch
stories.summary: Nieman Lab examines how rising event costs combined with falling funding are forcing journalism membership organizations to cancel conferences and reduce staff, reversing the post-pandemic rebound in in-person gatherings.

stories.headline: Democratic Congress could move to protect press freedom
stories.summary: Poynter reports that within 48 hours of Democrats winning control of both chambers, Senator Richard Blumenthal moved to demand FCC records as part of an investigation, signaling early steps Democrats may take on press-freedom oversight.

stories.headline: AI-generated local news site mixes up UK and US place names
stories.summary: Press Gazette identified six instances where an AI-generated local news operation confused place names, such as mixing up Enfield, Connecticut with Enfield in North London, highlighting quality-control risks in automated local journalism.

Media.gaps: Puck's site returned mostly older archived items beyond the 48-hour window aside from the Mary Hager story already captured via Status; CJR's only recent item was a roundup/commentary piece (Laurels and Darts) that didn't fit the newsworthiness criteria. NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block search, so only the single media-relevant feed item provided for WSJ (Cravath insider trading charge) could be used, and no qualifying media-industry items were found in the provided feed for NYT, FT or The Guardian.
